data.raw_response:
=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): opposite (clearly visible as paired leaves emerging from the same node along the stem in multiple images)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves appear grouped near the top of the visible stem, not widely spaced along its length)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf unit is a single blade without division into leaflets)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.): toothed (serrate) (clearly visible fine, regular teeth along the leaf edge)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): ovate to elliptic (broadest near the base, tapering toward the apex)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acuminate (tapers to a distinct, elongated tip)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): rounded to slightly cordate (appears broadly rounded or shallowly heart-shaped at the base)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (single midrib with secondary veins branching off laterally)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): clearly visible, moderately spaced, approximately 5-7 pairs visible on larger leaves
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): dull (lacks significant gloss; surface appears matte)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): present (fine hairs are clearly visible along the margins and on the stem surface in close-up views)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petioles are visibly shorter than the leaf blade)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (appears rounded in cross-section, no obvious wings or grooves)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): herbaceous (appears soft, green, and flexible, typical of young seedlings)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): present (fine hairs are visible along the stem, especially near nodes)
    19. Stem color: green to brownish-green (varies along the stem, greener near tips, browner lower down)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (no obvious ridges, grooves, or prominent lenticels visible)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): unclear (stipules, if present, are not clearly resolved in any image)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no latex exudate visible)
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no pulvinus structure visible at leaf bases)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no tendrils observed)
F. Notes: The seedling exhibits prominent serrate margins and fine trichomes on leaves and stems. Leaves are arranged oppositely. A yellow tag labeled "84" is wrapped around the stem in one image. Small holes are present on some leaves.
